summary:
Firebreak is a web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion data into source-linked evidence grades. Ask for a material and a cabin atmosphere — PMMA at ISS conditions, or Kevlar webbing on the lunar surface — and it answers four questions: what evidence exists, what A–D grade it supports, what uncertainty remains, and which test would change the answer.

It ranks all 11 NASA-named combustion investigations for ISS, airlock, lunar and spacesuit environments, tags each to prevention, detection or suppression, and explains every grade through a four-role evidence court built from rules, not a language model. Each claim links to a PSI test row, an NTRS page, or a NASA standard clause.

Why it matters: NASA's own BASS-II data show PMMA still spreading at 13.6% oxygen in microgravity — below the ~16% where it extinguishes in 1-g. Earth-qualified materials can fail in the wrong direction. Firebreak makes that transfer gap visible, and refuses to grade what the evidence cannot support: 0 of 8 material classes reach Grade A or B for lunar surface.
details:
1. DETAILED PROJECT DESCRIPTION

WHAT FIREBREAK DOES

Firebreak is an evidence-graded fire safety screening console for spacecraft materials. Ask for a material and a cabin atmosphere — PMMA at ISS conditions, or Kevlar webbing on the lunar surface — and it returns four answers: what evidence exists, what A–D grade that evidence supports, what uncertainty remains, and the single test that would change the result. It ranks all 11 NASA-named combustion investigations for ISS, airlock/Gateway, lunar and spacesuit environments, tags each to prevention, detection or suppression, and shows a four-role evidence court behind every grade. Every claim links to a PSI test row, an NTRS page or a NASA standard clause. It runs fully offline.

THE PROBLEM IT ANSWERS

In 1-g, PMMA stops burning near 16% oxygen. In microgravity, NASA's own BASS-II data show it still spreading at 13.6% — a negative margin of 2.4 percentage points. Materials qualified on Earth can therefore fail in the wrong direction on orbit. Engineers do not need another opinion; they need to know what the evidence covers and where it stops.

HOW IT WORKS — KEY TECHNICAL INNOVATIONS

  1. A–D Evidence Grading Engine. Ten versioned rules, each carrying a citation, assign a grade from source-linked rows. A grade requires reported pressure; when pressure is missing it stays missing and the grade is capped. A model never writes the grade.
  2. Investigation-Level Relevance Ranking. All 11 investigations the challenge names are ranked per crew environment, with the reasoning shown per investigation and each mapped to prevention, detection or suppression.
  3. Scoped Severity Model with Abstention. A monotonic gradient-boosted screen estimates BASS-II CO₂-rise severity and returns 80% conformal prediction sets. It abstains outside PMMA/SIBAL and 13.6–22.2% O₂ — including at the 24.1% ISS cabin preset — instead of extrapolating.
  4. Contradiction Detector. The console surfaces disagreement between 1-g and microgravity evidence, with the PMMA 2.4-point margin as the worked case.
  5. Offline-First Architecture. Retrieval, coverage checks, rules and citation are deterministic and local. An optional on-device language router only selects which tool to call; answers are built from tool output, so the system works with Wi-Fi disabled and no API keys.

2. NASA DATA AND EVIDENCE CHAIN

Firebreak ingests 1,170 curated records — 637 experiment rows plus 533 characterisation rows from SAME, SAME-R, FLEX, BASS and SLICE — together with 501 pages across nine NASA documents. Six pressure-bearing evidence anchors set the top grades. Every row is hashed and provenance-tracked, and each highlighted evidence set is labelled: characterisation records demonstrate detection and suppression coverage but never enter a grade.

3. WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

  1. The refusal is the product. "Grade D — the evidence does not support an answer" and "run this test" are first-class outputs, not error states. A system that declines to answer is harder to imitate than one that always does.
  2. A certainty framework for combustion evidence. To our knowledge no graded evidence framework exists for spacecraft flammability: NIST's material characterisation database reports measurements without grading, and GRADE is clinical. Firebreak applies that discipline to combustion evidence.
  3. The headline is a negative result. For lunar surface, 0 of 8 material classes reach Grade A or B. That is a finding about the state of the field, not a gap in the tool.

4. IMPACT AND WHO IT IS FOR

Firebreak sits at the front of a NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 campaign. It tells a materials engineer what is already anchored, where budget is being spent proving known conditions, and which environment is genuinely unanchored: ISS cabin anchors 2 of 8 material classes, while airlock and lunar surface anchor none, and the spacesuit case is deliberately not graded. Screening support only — not certification or flight approval.

5. HOW WE BUILT IT

Python 3.11, FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyMuPDF and vanilla JavaScript/CSS, with an optional local Cactus Needle router and Playwright for verification. The build is covered by 63 automated tests, a 60/60-field extraction audit, and a scoped severity screen at 0.811 AUC against a 0.605 O₂-only baseline.

6. FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

  1. Integrity over completeness. We refused to invent pressure values; instead we located the page-cited BASS-II passages that state pressure and ingested them as a separate, clearly labelled layer.
  2. Abstention over extrapolation. The severity model is scoped to PMMA/SIBAL and 13.6–22.2% O₂ and refuses queries outside its support.
  3. Determinism over generation. Rules assign grades, so every claim is auditable and reproducible.
  4. Characterisation is not evidence. 533 smoke-aerosol, droplet-extinction and test-log rows add detection and suppression coverage without adding a single flammability claim.

7. LIMITATIONS — STATED PLAINLY

Grade A currently covers PMMA and SIBAL; other materials cap at B or C. The severity model predicts one target (δCO₂ > 0.5) and does not predict ignition or flame spread. Firebreak is screening support, not certification. We do not claim superintelligence — we claim a system that ranks evidence, shows its reasoning, and refuses to answer when the data runs out.

TRY IT

Live console and guided demo: https://diyongamage.github.io/firebreak/?tour=1
Source code: https://github.com/DiyonGamage/firebreak
